title: Old Timers' Room
subtitle: Historic Photographs & Traditions Since 1881
transcript: You've entered the Old Timers' Room, where the photographs on display date back as far as 1881 — the year Deming was founded. In the early days of the railroad, the Santa Fe and Southern Pacific lines met just outside town to drive the silver spike completing the second transcontinental railroad. Steam locomotives of the era could only travel about 60 miles before needing to refill their water tanks, and as it happens, Deming sits almost exactly 60 miles from Las Cruces, Lordsburg, and Silver City alike. That made it a natural water stop — and the town grew up quickly around it. Around 1900, a group of Deming businessmen began an annual tradition: a lavish dinner party, hosted by a group who called themselves 'The Old Timers.' Over the years they built a growing collection of photographs, which they displayed in the windows of Mahoney's Hardware Store — the same collection now on view in this room, alongside a list of the Old Timers' Association presidents for the past 113 years. The wrought-iron photo racks holding them were built in the early 1980s by Harold Measday. The tradition continues to this day: the Deming Old Timers still gather every October for class reunions, a banquet, and a dance — making it the longest continuously running celebration in the state of New Mexico. Among the wrought-iron photographs, look for images of the Deming Harvey House and the Holy Cross Sanitarium. Other notable photos in the room include a framed picture of the great fire of July 11, 1918; the Deming High School class of 1932 yearbook; a photo of local doctor Paul Feil and his wife, Alma; the 1918 diploma of Frances Isabel Phillips; a faded photograph labeled '1902 picture of Horse & Buggy Days'; a portrait of Herman Perez, age 112 in 1928; and an artist's rendition of Deming in 1898, looking south down Gold Street toward the railroad station.

title: Mimbres Pottery & Prehistoric Culture
subtitle: Masterpieces of 950–1200 A.D. & Mogollon Heritage
transcript: About 5,000 Mimbres Indians lived along the Mimbres River and occupied the Deming, Silver City, and Lordsburg area—spanning Luna, Grant, and Hidalgo counties—from 950 to 1200 A.D. Fortunately, they buried pottery with their deceased under the floors of their homes. From archaeological excavations, we know the Mimbres were a deeply religious, agricultural people. Their painted pots depict wedding ceremonies, christenings, babies carried on cradleboards, children playing, and grandfathers telling stories. One famous bowl shows an elder with a cane and a hand on his back. Their pottery gives us extraordinary insight into their dress, hairstyles, weapons, ceremonial dancing, bird-snaring, and daily life. The circular hole in the center of burial pottery was ceremonial—known as 'killing' the pot to release the spirit of the vessel—often placed over the head of the deceased. Painted using chewed yucca leaf brushes and natural earth mineral pigments, Mimbres black-on-white and red-on-white pottery is internationally renowned. As archaeologist J.W. Fewkes observed, 'no Southwestern pottery, ancient or modern, surpasses that of the Mimbres.' Geographically, the Mimbres homeland was the only low-land route from the Atlantic to the Pacific without mountain navigation—the exact geographic reason why the southern transcontinental railroad and Interstate 10 were built right through Deming.
highlights: Chewed Yucca Leaf & Mineral Pigment Artistry

title: Main Room — Historic 1916 Armory
subtitle: The Building's Story & Architecture
transcript: Welcome to the Main Room of the Deming Luna Mimbres Museum! You are standing inside the historic 1916 red-brick National Guard Armory, listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Originally built for the New Mexico National Guard Company I during a time of intense Southwestern border tensions, this building was later converted into a community center and museum by the Luna County Historical Society. As you walk through the exhibits, notice the heavy exposed timber roof trusses, soaring ceilings, and original brickwork that have witnessed over a century of Deming and Southwest history.

title: Military Room
subtitle: Honoring Service, Bataan, WWII Airfield & Frontier Forts
transcript: Welcome to the Military Room. Along the left wall are photographs of Luna County residents who served in the various branches of our Armed Forces, and the cabinets around you hold insignia, uniforms, mementos, and challenge coins donated and loaned by local families. Look for the faded black-and-white photo of the 200th and 515th Coast Artillery—the New Mexico servicemen who would later take part in the Bataan Death March. A full exhibit on the march is located near the museum's entrance. In the World War II section, you'll find uniforms, insignia, and mementos donated by veterans and their families, along with scale models of ships and planes. At the center of the room, a plexiglass case holds a Norden Mark XV Bombsight—the same model tested in B-17 bombers that trained right here at the Deming Army Airfield, where nearly 8,000 bombardiers were trained by the end of the war. Next, explore displays devoted to Fort Cummings, the first walled fort in New Mexico Territory (1863–1873) and home to the 9th and 10th Cavalry 'Buffalo Soldiers'. Learn about Camp Cody, Deming's massive WWI training camp named after Buffalo Bill Cody, which later became a tuberculosis sanitarium. Finally, view artifacts from the March 9, 1916 Pancho Villa Raid on Columbus, NM, including the historic machine gun that defended the town and General John J. Pershing's Punitive Expedition gear.
highlights: Deming Army Airfield Norden Bombsight & B-17s
Camp Cody WWI Camp & Holy Cross Sanitarium
March 9, 1916 Columbus Raid Defense Machine Gun

title: Bataan Death March Display
subtitle: 200th & 515th Coast Artillery Anti-Aircraft Heroes
transcript: This case is dedicated to the 200th & 515th Coast Artillery Anti-Aircraft Corps. Between April 9 and April 17, 1942, the Imperial Japanese Army forced roughly 75,000 American and Filipino prisoners of war on a 65-mile march from Mariveles to Camp O'Donnell on the Bataan Peninsula. The prisoners received almost no food or water, and thousands did not survive. They endured severe physical abuse, beatings, and torture. The Bataan Death March struck close to home in Deming: many of the American soldiers captured at Bataan came from New Mexico. The 200th & 515th Coast Artillery units numbered 1,816 men total—829 died in battle, in captivity, or shortly after liberation, and 987 survived. Since 1989, the Bataan Memorial Death March—a marathon-length, 26.2-mile march and run—has been held each spring at White Sands Missile Range in their memory. The cabinets around you hold newspaper articles and photographs donated by Deming-area POWs and their families. The large, framed plaque in the right-hand cabinet lists 83 Luna County residents who served in the 200th & 515th Coast Artillery; thirty of them were killed in action. Nearby is a shadowbox donated by the family of Lee Gardner.
highlights: Deming POW Personal Letters, Photos & Shadowboxes
Annual Bataan Memorial Death March (White Sands)

title: Doll & Toy Room
subtitle: Auburn Rubber, Historic Dolls & Childhood Memories
transcript: The doll and toy room is unique as we have toys made from the pioneers settling in Luna County and from Auburn Rubber—the largest producer of rubber and vinyl toys in America and probably the world. They moved their molds from Auburn, Indiana to Deming in the 1959–1960 timeframe. We have a doll from the Pancho Villa Raid of March 9, 1916. The doll belonged to the daughter of the telephone operator who called in the raid. Glass shards rained on the daughter's head as bullets broke the window above the area where she was sleeping. We also have a Japanese doll from the ashes of Hiroshima. The hair is real from a Japanese woman; an American soldier picked the doll from a pile of rubbish and later donated it to our museum. A walk through this room will bring back childhood memories of toys you may have likely played with as a child. This room and the adjoining Old Timers' Room you just walked through were originally a small-caliber indoor shooting range used by the soldiers stationed here. During World War II, when this building served as a USO, these two rooms were converted to a bowling alley.
highlights: Armory Shooting Range & WWII USO Bowling Alley

title: Transportation Annex
subtitle: Harvey House, 1904 REO, Fire Truck & Railroad History
transcript: Transportation has shaped life in Deming and throughout the Southwest for generations. From wagons and railroads to automobiles and modern highways, each advancement changed how people traveled, worked, traded, and stayed connected. On March 18, 1881, the Santa Fe and Southern Pacific Railroad met to create the southern transcontinental railroad line, joining east and west with a silver spike. Charles Crocker was one of the four railroad barons, and Deming was named after his wife, Mary Deming-Crocker. Deming boasted one of the grandest Harvey Houses in the Southwest—America's first restaurant chain—where single young women of good character, known as Harvey Girls, served gourmet meals on silver and fine china. Our exhibit preserves original lumber and paint from Deming's historic Harvey House, donated by Santa Fe employees. You'll also see the original sign from Deming's historic train station, Deming's first volunteer fire truck (go ahead and ring the bell or turn the siren handle!), the 1904 REO—the very first automobile owned by a Deming resident—and two classic soap box derby cars raced in El Paso.
highlights: Historic Harvey House & Harvey Girls Display
Original Deming Train Station Sign & Railroad Gear
Deming's First Volunteer Fire Truck with Working Bell & Siren
1904 REO Automobile & Historic Soap Box Derby Racers

title: Medical Room
subtitle: Historic Healthcare, 1940s/50s Iron Lungs & Deming Sanitaria
transcript: This room may be difficult for some visitors, as it illustrates the medical practices and equipment once in everyday use. The items on display were donated by doctors and hospitals that served Deming from the 1930s through the 1950s. Among the most striking pieces are two iron lungs — an adult version and a child's — donated by the former Deming Memorial Hospital, where they were used during the polio epidemics of 1949 and 1952. The hospital contributed many other medical items on display here as well. You'll also find a wooden birthing chair from Spain, along with artifacts from hospitals and clinics throughout the Deming area, including the Ladies Hospital, Faywood Hot Springs, the Camp Cody Red Cross Building and Infirmary, and Holy Cross Hospital, which operated for many years as a tuberculosis sanitarium. The nun doll on display was donated by the Holy Cross Order of South Bend, Indiana, along with a research paper detailing the order's history establishing and running the Holy Cross Sanitarium in Deming. Medicine has come a long way since these tools were in daily use.
highlights: Camp Cody Red Cross Infirmary & Faywood Hot Springs
Holy Cross Tuberculosis Sanitarium & Sister Doll

title: Western Area
subtitle: Ranching Life, Diamond A Chuckwagon & Ruebush Saddlery
transcript: Deming was founded as a railroad town that soon expanded into a booming agriculture hub for farming and ranching. Ranchers would spend days, even weeks riding the range in all elements of our environment, tending to their herds. To get the job of branding and gathering cattle for shipping on the railroad, packing the right equipment and supplies was crucial. The chuckwagon on display is from the historic Diamond A Ranch located in Hachita, New Mexico, and was built from multiple parts of other wagons. Many meals were served from this wagon to hungry cowboys; cast-iron pans, Dutch ovens, a boiling pot, water barrel, and branding irons were carefully loaded aboard. Staples consisting of flour, cornmeal, pinto beans, green coffee beans, salt pork, beef jerky, and bacon sustained crews on long cattle drives. This chuckwagon was last used on a drive in 1972. One of the most important parts of a rancher's comfort is his saddle—the majority of saddles on display were made locally in the early 1930s and 1940s by Ruebush Saddlery, located on Silver Street until the late 1970s. The cowboy hats were donated by local ranching families; it was said that the distinctive crease, brim, and tilt of a hat let cowboys recognize each other from far across the range.
highlights: Historic Diamond A Ranch Chuckwagon (Hachita, NM)
Last Used on a Cattle Drive in 1972
Luna County Registered Branding Irons & Tack
Donated Southwestern Cowboy Hats & Chuckwagon Gear

title: Quilt & Lace Room
subtitle: Hand-Stitched Heritage, 1820s Spreads & Lottie Deno Lace
transcript: European settlers — the Dutch and English among them — brought the tradition of quilting to America in the 17th century. Early quilts were practical creations, often pieced together from fabric scraps and recycled clothing. Over time, quilting bees became cherished social gatherings, giving women a chance to work side by side, trade stories, and strengthen the bonds of their community. The oldest quilt in this room is a hand-woven spread dating to around 1820, donated in memory of Bessie Gomer May, the woman largely responsible for this museum's existence. Look closely and you'll also find fine examples of tatting lace, made from an intricate series of knots and loops. One piece of particular interest is an altar cloth made by Lottie 'Deno' Thurman — known formally as Mrs. Frank Thurman. Lottie led a colorful life in Deming and was renowned as a remarkably shrewd gambler; her reputation was so notable that she's said to have inspired the character of Miss Kitty on the television series Gunsmoke. Several books on Lottie Deno's life are available online, or ask about them in our Gift Store.
highlights: Circa 1820 Hand-Woven Spread (Bessie Gomer May Memorial)
Inspiration for Miss Kitty of TV's Gunsmoke

title: Main Street Display
subtitle: Historic Storefronts, 1890s Hearse & The Deming Headlight
transcript: Upon this location's opening, the museum started to receive so many donations that it ran out of room and discussions were held to add additions. One such discussion was to recreate a storefront exhibit of Deming. What you see first are horse-drawn carriages: a hearse donated by Baca Funeral Home last used in the 90s; buggies used for going to church and courting; a sleigh, even though Deming only receives an average of nine inches of precipitation per year; and various wagons used by families, farmers, and ranchers. To the right of the hearse is Deming's first traffic light and an old gas pump. The recreated shops illustrate what items were available: Mahoney Hardware houses the washing machine that sparked the founding of this museum; alongside a dental office, beauty salon, dress shop, post office, livery stable, funeral parlor with an antique casket, and barber shop with original storefront signs. The Deming Headlight is of particular interest as the oldest continuously published newspaper in the state; look in the window to see an antique typewriter, an over-engineered pencil sharpener, and their original, massive vintage printing press.
highlights: Baca Funeral Home 1890s Horse-Drawn Hearse & Sleigh
Deming's First Working Traffic Light & Vintage Gas Pump
Mahoney Hardware & The Museum-Founding Washing Machine
Recreated Main Street Shops: Barber, Dentist, Millinery & Post Office
The Deming Headlight Newspaper & Heavy Antique Printing Press

title: Geodes Display
subtitle: The Geode Kid Collection, Thundereggs & Agates
transcript: Welcome to the Geode Room! The Geode Kid Collection brings together geodes, thundereggs, petrified wood, fossils, and other minerals from across the region—many collected right here in Luna County and the surrounding Mimbres Valley area. A geode is a spherical rock formed inside sedimentary or volcanic stone, hiding a hollow chamber lined with sparkling crystals. Those crystals grow when mineral-rich water seeps into small cavities, called vesicles, within volcanic rock and slowly fills them in over millennia. Nearby Rockhound State Park, just southeast of Deming, is one of the rare state parks in the country where visitors are welcome to take home what they find! Rockhounds regularly discover agates and thundereggs: nodules formed in rhyolitic volcanic ash beds. Slice and polish a thunderegg, and you will find centers of chalcedony with bands of agate, jasper, or opal, alongside quartz and gypsum crystals. While a geode is defined by its hollow crystal center, a thunderegg is a unique solid or crystal-filled nodule—and nature has created countless masterpieces right beneath Luna County's soil.
highlights: The Geode Kid Mineral & Fossil Collection
Rockhound State Park Legal Collecting Area

title: Pancho Villa Raid & Border History
subtitle: The 1916 Columbus Raid
transcript: On March 9, 1916, Mexican revolutionary General Francisco 'Pancho' Villa launched a surprise raid on the town of Columbus, NM, just 30 miles south of Deming. In response, President Woodrow Wilson dispatched General John J. 'Black Jack' Pershing on the Punitive Expedition into Mexico. This room houses weapons, photographs, military dispatches, and artifacts from Camp Furlong and the border conflict.

title: Deming Fire Department & Early Services
subtitle: Protecting the Frontier Town
transcript: In a town built largely of wood and dry adobe during the railroad era, fire protection was a matter of life and death. This gallery showcases early hand-drawn hose carts, brass fire extinguishers, leather helmets, and the original alarm bells that alerted Deming's volunteer firefighters to emergencies across town.

title: Custom House & Historic Outbuildings
subtitle: Border Commerce & Customs
transcript: Thank you for completing the tour! Outside the main armory stands the historic Custom House, managed by the museum. Built during the era when international trade passed between Mexico and New Mexico territory, it preserves office records, customs stamps, and boundary survey equipment that shaped the border region.
